children: Shares of domestic airlines IndiGo and SpiceJet were trading in the red on Tuesday morning following the latest revision in Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices.

InterGlobe Aviation, the parent company of IndiGo, was trading at Rs 5,087.50 on the NSE at 9:35 am, down Rs 146.50, or 2.80%, from the previous close. SpiceJet shares were trading at Rs 10.23, down Rs 0.09, or 0.87%.
ATF prices for domestic airlines were hiked 5.46% for the second consecutive month on Tuesday, with Aviation Turbine Fuel prices rising by Rs 6.28 per litre to Rs 121.28 per litre from Rs 115.

The latest increase follows a 7.5% hike in ATF prices last month. The two consecutive increases come after three monthly reductions in ATF prices starting April 2025. Prices had been cut by Rs 12,239.17 per kilolitre across those three reductions, while the subsequent increases of Rs 8,949.38 per kilolitre have wiped away almost three-fourths of the gains.
Fuel accounts for almost 40% of an airline's operating costs, making changes in ATF prices an important factor for carriers.

ATF prices vary from city to city depending on local taxes such as VAT. In August, prices were raised to Rs 86,077.14 per kilolitre in Mumbai, Rs 95,512.26 per kilolitre in Chennai and Rs 95,164.90 per kilolitre in Kolkata.

State-owned Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) revise ATF and cooking gas prices on the first of every month, based on the average price of benchmark international fuel and foreign exchange rates.
Domestic petrol and diesel prices continue to remain unchanged.

title: IndiGo, SpiceJet shares fall up to 3% after ATF hike for second month in a row
